meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Who decided on the zero, and did anyone hear Owen first?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Was Owen heard before you entered it?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58, I'm writing those down. Plenty of kids write somewhere else and paste it in. What else?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Fine. Whatever comes of this, it stays off his record and it stays out of his classroom. Is anything on his file right now?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Seventeen-year-olds get Shakespeare wrong all the time. And you skipped my question, Hale: is anything on his file?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Then I'll take your word on the play, for now. What are you proposing, and put in writing that nothing is on his file.
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
An outline is where a student starts, not where he's obliged to end up. You're laying out a case, Hale, and still not telling me what you want.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Okay. He'll sit it to put this behind him, not because he did anything. Private, before December 1, nothing on his file, and I want that email tonight with the apology in it.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
I'll ask him tonight and reply to your email. Put Thursday the twelfth in it.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4, after school and not in front of his class, before December 1, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record, and you proposed Thursday, November 12 after school. I still want that in writing, with your apology for entering the zero before anyone called me, and written confirmation that nothing is on his file right now. I expect that email tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Last position; she agreed to a private supervised rewrite under 4.4 before December 1, with Thursday the twelfth pending Owen. She still wants your email tonight with the apology and confirmation that nothing is on his file. That is the fair outcome, and you reached it before her time ran out.
What moved her: You showed the version history with its exact times and then answered her pasting defence by offering to look at any dated earlier draft, which gave her something specific she could check.
What cost ground: You never answered her question about whether anything was on his file, even though she asked it twice, so her one non-negotiable stayed open longer than it needed to.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your version history, showing the document built between 11:31 and 11:58 PM the night before it was due, landed close to that late-night memory. It proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked whether anything was on his file, answer it plainly right then, before you show her the outline.
